comments.author: @Investigacions
comments.text:
Actually Mexico almost participated in World War One.

In World War One, Germany tried to persuade Mexico to join the war against the United States through the Zimmermann Telegram of 1917. Germany proposed supporting Mexico in recovering the territory that had belonged to Mexico just 65 years before.  This included all or part of the following US States:
California, Nevada, Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, Texas, Colorado, Wyoming, Kansas and Oklahoma

Many dismiss the idea that Mexico could have influenced World War I had it accepted Germany's proposal in the Zimmermann Telegram. However, Germany's objective was not for Mexico to defeat the United States, but to force it to divert troops and resources from Europe to defend its southern border. 

Even today, despite immense resources and modern technology, controlling all cross-border movement remains difficult. A military conflict with German troops based in Mexico, it would have required the deployment of additional troops and resources to protect transportation networks, infrastructure, harbors and border communities.

A conflict along the U.S.-Mexico border would have required significant military and economic resources, potentially delaying the American war effort overseas. From Germany's perspective, even a limited war could have served as a strategic distraction.
